title: Six Rules, Six Shapes! Graphs Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
One sheet of graph paper, six simple rules and six completely different shapes: a slanted line, a flat line, a U, an S bend, a V and two curves that never touch the axes. Looking only at a shape, can you tell which rule drew it? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 2, Relations and Functions) we learn how the graphs of the standard functions are built and how to read them.

You will watch a table of values turn into a parabola point by point, see y = x to the power n morph live from a line into a U and then an S bend as n counts up, compare x squared with x cubed, and read domain and range by shining a light onto the axes. Then we tell the U of x squared from the V of mod x and find where they meet. Two pause-and-think questions, the exam trap about the range on an interval, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 One sheet, six shapes
0:25 Every graph starts as a table
0:53 Identity and constant functions
1:09 Live: y = x^n as n counts up
1:31 x squared vs x cubed
2:09 Read domain and range from the shadows
2:40 The U vs the V
3:13 Worked example: where the U meets the V
3:51 Exam trap: range on an interval
4:08 Where it is asked
4:17 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:49 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 23): Combining and Comparing Functions. A canteen bill adds the cost of tea and a snack: can we add two functions?
